items.q: The adequacy-of-compensation flowchart is built around which quantity?
opts: The compensatory metabolite, compared with its expected and normal values
The anion gap, compared with 12 mEq/L
The base excess, compared with zero
items.exp: The flowchart tracks the compensatory metabolite, comparing it with the expected value and with the normal value. (Book p828)

items.q: Match the compensation verdicts for metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis — 1) ≤ expected value  2) Between expected and normal value  3) Group of disorders this arm covers … A) Partial compensation  B) Metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis  C) Adequate compensation
items.exp: In metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis, a compensatory metabolite ≤ expected value = adequate compensation, while a value between expected and normal = partial compensation. (Book p828)

items.q: Match the compensation verdicts for metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis — 1) ≥ expected value  2) Between expected and normal value  3) Group of disorders this arm covers … A) Metabolic alkalosis and respiratory acidosis  B) Adequate compensation  C) Partial compensation
items.exp: For metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis the mirrored rule applies: ≥ expected value = adequate compensation, between expected and normal = partial compensation. (Book p828)

items.q: A patient with metabolic acidosis has a compensatory metabolite that lies exactly between the expected value and the normal value. What does the flowchart call this?
items.exp: A compensatory metabolite between the expected and normal values is labelled partial compensation in both arms of the flowchart. (Book p828)

items.q: ‘The two arms of the compensation flowchart are mirror images: ≤ expected value is adequate in one arm and ≥ expected value is adequate in the other.’
opts: True — metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis use ≤ and metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis use ≥
False — both arms use ≤ expected value for adequate compensation
False — both arms use ≥ expected value for adequate compensation
True, except that partial compensation is defined differently in the two arms
items.exp: The flowchart is mirrored: ≤ expected value = adequate for metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis, while ≥ expected value = adequate for metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis; between expected and normal = partial in both. (Book p828)

items.q: All but one of these pairings of the two compensation arms are printed. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Metabolic alkalosis and respiratory acidosis — adequate compensation when ≤ expected value
Metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis — adequate compensation when ≤ expected value
Metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis — partial compensation when between expected and normal
Metabolic alkalosis and respiratory acidosis — adequate compensation when ≥ expected value
items.exp: The ≥ expected value rule belongs to the metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis arm; the ≤ rule belongs to the metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis arm. (Book p828)
